instruction: Make the title 'H2O—Soak up the Science' bold in the document.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully selected the '2' character in 'H2O' title and applied subscript formatting via Format > Text > Subscript menu, then saved the document. Completed in 11 turns.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can select specific characters in LibreOffice Writer, navigate Format menu, apply text formatting (subscript), save documents
metadata.task_rationale: Since the model successfully applied subscript formatting to the title, this variation tests a related formatting operation (bold) on the same title paragraph.
metadata.explanation: Task requires selecting the title and applying bold formatting. Getter reads the docx file and checks if all runs in the title paragraph (index 1) have bold=True. Metric compares actual bold status to expected.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads the docx file and checks paragraph index 1 (the title 'H2O—Soak up the Science') for bold formatting across all runs.
Metric correctly handles expected parameter: since expected.type='rule', get_rule returns {'expected_bold': true} directly, and metric accesses expected.get('expected_bold', True) correctly.
Postconfig properly saves the document (Ctrl+S) before the getter reads the file, ensuring fresh state.
Full coverage: the single instruction requirement (make title bold) is completely verified.

Minor concern: run.font.bold can be None (inherited from paragraph style) rather than True. The check 'if not run.font.bold' treats None as falsy, which could cause a false negative if bold is applied via style inheritance rather than direct formatting. However, typical Ctrl+B application sets run.font.bold=True explicitly, so this is unlikely to be an issue in practice.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider checking for run.font.bold being None (style-inherited bold) in addition to True, e.g., treat None as potentially bold if the paragraph style itself is bold.
